extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO (trademark and other non-patent matters), OED/disciplinary participants
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order approving an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. §11.27, excluding a practitioner on consent from practice before the USPTO in trademark and non-patent matters and describing applicable rules, alleged violations, required compliance, and publication obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation compliance (37 C.F.R. §11.27(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. §11.27(a); the Director may approve an affidavit and exclude a respondent on consent if the affidavit meets those requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order states the OED Director determined the Affidavit of Resignation complies with §11.27(a) and therefore approved it and ordered exclusion on consent. The affidavit must show consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and the respondent is aware of the pending disciplinary matter and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of consenting to exclusion (effect on reinstatement presumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: By consenting to exclusion under §11.27, the respondent acknowledges that if and when she applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. §11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of determining the reinstatement application, that (a) the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true, and (b) she could not have successfully defended herself against those allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a collateral consequence of approving an affidavit of resignation and is explicitly acknowledged in the affidavit and the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner eligibility to represent others before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an attorney active and in good standing with the highest court of a State may represent others before the Office in trademark and other non-patent matters (37 C.F.R. §11.1 and 37 C.F.R. §11.14(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not licensed and in good standing, a person is not authorized to practice before the Office in trademark matters; practicing while suspended or not in good standing is unauthorized practice (see also §11.505).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature requirement for trademark filings (37 C.F.R. §2.193)
rubrics_metrics.description: The person named as the signatory on an electronic trademark document filed with the Office must personally enter his or her electronic signature on the document (i.e., personally enter the combination of letters, numbers, spaces and/or punctuation marks adopted as a signature, placed between two forward slash ('/') symbols in the signature block).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited regs: 37 C.F.R. §2.193(a)(2), (c), and (e). The Final Order finds respondent impermissibly entered clients' electronic signatures on multiple trademark documents, rendering those documents filed with false signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: TMEP guidance on personal entry of electronic signature (TMEP §611.01(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: TMEP advises: 'All documents must be personally signed. The person(s) identified as the signatory must manually enter the elements of the electronic signature. Another person (e.g., paralegal, legal assistant, or secretary) may not sign the name of a qualified practitioner or other authorized signatory. Typing the electronic signature of another person is not a valid signature by that person.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order quotes TMEP §611.01(c) language to support that typing another's electronic signature is not a valid signature; this practice can lead to disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declarations warnings and false statements (18 U.S.C. §1001)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark declarations typically warn that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. §1001 and may jeopardize the validity of the application or registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order reproduces the common declaration language warning signatories about penalties for willful false statements and the legal consequences for filing falsehoods in trademark submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. §11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in the unauthorized practice of law before the USPTO in trademark matters is prohibited (37 C.F.R. §11.505).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order alleges and relies on respondent's practice while suspended or otherwise ineligible as unauthorized practice; this is a basis for disciplinary action and exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to reasonably consult with client (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished; failure to do so is a violation (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director alleged this failure as part of the disciplinary complaint; such failures can support discipline or exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to keep client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter; failing to do so violates §11.104(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged in the complaint and cited in the Final Order as a professional-conduct violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to consult about limitations on practitioner's conduct (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the practitioner knows the client expects assistance not permitted by the USPTO Rules or other law, the practitioner must consult with the client about any relevant limitation on the practitioner's conduct (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to warn or consult about such limitations is a listed violation in the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to explain to permit informed decisions (37 C.F.R. §11.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation (37 C.F.R. §11.104(b)); failing to do so is misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in the complaint as part of the basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to withdraw when representation would violate rules or law (37 C.F.R. §11.116(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must withdraw from representation of a client if the representation will result in violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or other law (37 C.F.R. §11.116(a)(1)); failure to withdraw is a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged in the complaint where respondent continued to act while ineligible to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation is proscribed (37 C.F.R. §11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing documents with false signatures is an example of conduct that may fall under this provision and supports disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged as a basis for discipline in the complaint and referenced in the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other conduct adversely reflecting on practitioner's fitness (37 C.F.R. §11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must avoid conduct that otherwise adversely reflects on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO (37 C.F.R. §11.804(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites this catch-all as among the provisions the OED Director believes were violated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations following exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette that is materially consistent with the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs electronic publication at the OED Reading Room URL and provides sample Official Gazette notice text summarizing the exclusion, allegations, and findings (including signature and unauthorized-practice issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 as ordered in the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order explicitly directs compliance; §11.58 concerns duties and obligations applicable to excluded practitioners (e.g., notice obligations and restrictions while excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 upon reinstatement request
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. §11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §11.60 governs reinstatement procedures and eligibility; the Final Order requires full compliance with that provision when/if respondent seeks reinstatement.
